assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock, built on Katori's magic-wavelength proposal, removes recoil and Doppler shifts while interrogating thousands of atoms at once. It has taken fractional uncertainty to the 1e-18 level and opened clock-based tests of fundamental physics and relativistic geodesy. As an atomic physicist I regard the underlying atomic-structure insight (state-independent trapping) as original and clear.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed and first demonstrated the magic-wavelength lattice concept. Ye's JILA group pushed the performance frontier and the many-body and spectroscopic control. Two names give a clean, defensible configuration; other groups (for example NIST, PTB, SYRTE) are important but secondary.
assessment.maturity: Very mature: multiple independent labs reproduce and compare clocks at the 1e-18 level, and a redefinition of the second based on optical standards is under discussion. Timing is good, since the 2005 and 2012 prizes honoured combs and single-ion control, which this builds on without duplicating.
uncertainties: Exact attribution of the first demonstrations (strontium versus ytterbium versus other species) is something I cannot verify here.
Overlap with earlier recognition of frequency combs and ion clocks could be argued, though the lattice concept is distinct.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect and the Z2 topological insulator, followed by the HgTe observation of helical edge transport, opened a large field of topological band theory and materials. The conceptual clarity is high and the impact on condensed matter physics is lasting.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele supplied the decisive theory (graphene QSH and the Z2 classification); Molenkamp's group delivered the experimental realisation in HgTe wells, following the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal. Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang (and Moore, Fu) are not in the credited list, so the credit is imperfect but a three-person prize is workable.
assessment.maturity: Mature: more than fifteen years of independent confirmation across HgTe, Bi-based 3D insulators and ARPES, with the interpretation stable. Recognition is arguably overdue relative to the 2016 topological-phases prize, which was about different ideas.
uncertainties: Allocation between the 2D QSH and 3D topological insulator work, and the role of non-credited theorists, is unresolved.
Whether the 2016 prize leaves room for a second topological award is a judgement I cannot settle.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED establishes strong coupling of microwave photons to superconducting artificial atoms and provides the dispersive readout and control architecture behind superconducting quantum processors. It is original, conceptually clean (cavity QED transplanted to a chip) and technologically decisive.
assessment.attribution: Blais and colleagues proposed the circuit QED architecture with Girvin and others; Wallraff and Schoelkopf demonstrated strong coupling in 2004. Steven Girvin and Rob Schoelkopf as theory-experiment pairing is a notable consideration, and Girvin is not in the credited names, so the allocation is somewhat uncertain.
assessment.maturity: Mature in the sense of independent reproduction and wide adoption; the field is moving quickly, and the 2025 prize on macroscopic circuit quantum tunnelling is closely related, which could argue for waiting or for treating this as a natural follow-on.
uncertainties: Proximity to the 2025 prize may reduce room for another superconducting-circuit award so soon.
Credit among the early proposers (Blais, Girvin, Huang, Wallraff, Schoelkopf and others) is contested at the margins.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of flat bands at a magic angle and the discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene created the moire quantum-materials field. It is a strikingly original, tunable platform for correlated physics.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the key theoretical prediction; Jarillo-Herrero's group made the decisive experimental discovery in 2018. Other groups (for example Dean, Young, Yazdani, Efetov) matter for the subsequent developments, but the three credited names fit the core discovery well.
assessment.maturity: Relatively young (2018) but replicated widely and the field is rapidly growing; the full interpretation of the superconducting phase and fractional Chern states is still evolving, so a prize could be seen as slightly early.
uncertainties: Mechanism of superconductivity in magic-angle graphene is not settled.
Possible need to recognise later fractional Chern insulator and quantum anomalous Hall results in moire systems separately.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum simulation with ultracold atoms in optical lattices (Bose-Hubbard proposal, superfluid-Mott transition, single-site quantum gas microscopy) gives controllable realisations of many-body models. This is original and important for the study of strongly correlated matter, and it sits close to my own field of atomic physics.
assessment.attribution: Zoller (with Jaksch, Cirac and colleagues) supplied the key proposals, Bloch and Greiner the experimental realisations including the Mott transition and microscopes. Cirac and Hofstetter and others contributed to the theory; I choose three only for a feasible prize.
assessment.maturity: Mature: broad independent confirmation by many groups over two decades, and quantum gas microscopes are standard. Some conceptual overlap with the 2001 BEC prize and with the Cirac-Zoller entries elsewhere on the list.
uncertainties: Allocation between Zoller and Cirac across this candidate and the trapped-ion candidate is unresolved.
Whether quantum simulation has yet produced a decisive result unreachable by classical methods remains open.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamical mean-field theory, exact in infinite dimensions, provides the standard non-perturbative framework for Mott transitions and correlated materials, and combined with ab initio methods it underlies much quantitative work on correlated electrons.
assessment.attribution: Metzner and Vollhardt founded the infinite-dimension limit; Georges and Kotliar built the DMFT mapping onto an impurity problem. Credit is shared and Metzner is not among the credited names, so the configuration is imperfect but still defensible.
assessment.maturity: Mature: three decades of use and cross-validation against experiment, although accuracy in finite dimensions and for cuprates remains debated.
uncertainties: The omission of Walter Metzner from the credited list weakens the attribution case.
A theory-only prize would need to rest on demonstrated predictive impact.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Cirac-Zoller proposal for quantum gates with trapped ions and the experimental demonstration of multi-qubit entangling operations and algorithms established a leading platform for quantum computing. It is important and clear, and it is close to atomic physics.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller made the theoretical proposal; Blatt's group led key experimental demonstrations. Wineland and Monroe are central for ion gates and are not on this credited list; Wineland already holds a 2012 prize for ion control.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with independent confirmation by several laboratories, but overlap with the 2012 prize and with the optical-lattice candidate complicates timing and credit.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2012 prize and with the other Cirac-Zoller candidates is unresolved.
Absence of Monroe and Wineland from the credited names makes attribution incomplete.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum key distribution (BB84 and E91) is a conceptually elegant use of quantum mechanics for secure communication, with a large conceptual impact on quantum information science.
assessment.attribution: Bennett and Brassard authored BB84; Ekert independently proposed the entanglement-based protocol. The credit is clear and a three-person prize is natural.
assessment.maturity: Mature conceptually, with decades of experimental demonstration, but the 2022 prize on entanglement experiments recognised an adjacent area, and the practical security of deployed systems remains a topic of debate.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2022 prize and the question of whether this is physics rather than information theory.
Real-world security and deployment status are not something I can verify.
